source.title: Some Open Problems on Locally Finite or Locally Nilpotent Derivations and E-Derivations

accepted.question_text: Let R be a commutative ring, let A be an R-algebra, and let δ be either an R-derivation of A or an R-E-derivation of A, where an R-E-derivation means an R-linear map of the form I − φ for some R-algebra endomorphism φ of A. For an R-subspace V of A, write r(V) for the set of elements a in A such that a^m lies in V for all sufficiently large m; and say that V is a left, right, or two-sided Mathieu subspace when eventual membership of all powers a^m forces eventual membership of ba^m, a^mc, or ba^mc respectively. The LFNED problem asks for a description of r(δ(I)) for every left, right, or two-sided ideal I of A, asks which R-derivations and R-E-derivations of A have image Im δ = δ(A) that is a Mathieu subspace of the corresponding handedness, and asks which such maps send every left, right, or two-sided ideal I of A to a Mathieu subspace of the corresponding handedness.

evidence.quote: Definition 1.1. Let ϑ represent the words: left, right, or two-sided. An R-subspace V of an R-algebra A is said to be a ϑ-Mathieu subspace (ϑ-MS) of A if for all a, b, c ∈ A with a^m ∈ V for all m ≥ 1, the following conditions hold: 1) ba^m ∈ V for all m ≫ 0, if ϑ = left; 2) a^mc ∈ V for all m ≫ 0, if ϑ = right; 3) ba^mc ∈ V for all m ≫ 0, if ϑ = two-sided.
Definition 1.2. [Z3, p. 247] Let V be an R-subspace of an R-algebra A. We define the radical of V , denoted by r(V ), to be the set of a ∈ A such that a^m ∈ V for all m ≫ 0.

Problem 1.4 (LFNED Problem). Let R be a commutative base ring, A an R-algebra and δ an R-derivation or R-E-derivation of A. A) Find the radical of δ(I) for all one-sided or two sided ideals I of A. B) Decide which R-derivations and R-E-derivations of A have the image being a ϑ-MS of A. C) Decide which R-derivations and R-E-derivations of A map every ϑ-ideal of A to a ϑ-MS of A.

accepted.question_text: Let K be a field of characteristic zero and let A be a K-algebra. If δ is a locally finite K-derivation or a locally finite K-E-derivation of A, where locally finite means that for every a in A the K-submodule spanned by δ^i(a) for i ≥ 0 is finitely generated, must the image Im δ = δ(A) always be a two-sided Mathieu subspace of A?

evidence.quote: An R-linear endomorphism η of A is said to be locally nilpotent (LN) if for each a ∈ A there exists m ≥ 1 such that η^m(a) = 0, and locally finite (LF) if for each a ∈ A the R-submodule spanned by η^i(a) (i ≥ 0) over R is finitely generated.

Conjecture 1.5 (The LFED Conjecture). Let K be a field of characteristic zero and A a K-algebra. Then for every locally finite K-derivation or locally finite K-E-derivation δ of A, the image Im δ := δ(A) of δ is a (two-sided) MS of A.

accepted.question_text: Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let δ be either a locally nilpotent K-derivation of A or a locally nilpotent K-E-derivation of A, where locally nilpotent means that for every a in A there exists m ≥ 1 with δ^m(a) = 0. For each choice of handedness ϑ ∈ {left, right, two-sided}, if I is a ϑ-ideal of A, must the image δ(I) always be a ϑ-Mathieu subspace of A?

evidence.quote: An R-linear endomorphism η of A is said to be locally nilpotent (LN) if for each a ∈ A there exists m ≥ 1 such that η^m(a) = 0, and locally finite (LF) if for each a ∈ A the R-submodule spanned by η^i(a) (i ≥ 0) over R is finitely generated.

Conjecture 1.6 (The LNED Conjecture). Let K be a field of characteristic zero, A a K-algebra and δ a locally nilpotent K-derivation or a locally nilpotent K-E-derivation of A. Then for every ϑ-ideal I of A, the image δ(I) of I under δ is a ϑ-MS of A.

accepted.question_text: Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let δ be a K-derivation or K-E-derivation of A. If δ is locally finite, does every idempotent e in Im δ force the principal ideal (e) generated by e to lie inside Im δ? If δ is locally nilpotent, does every idempotent e in δ(I), for every left, right, or two-sided ideal I of A, force the corresponding left, right, or two-sided ideal generated by e to lie inside δ(I)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1.7 (The Idempotent Conjecture). Let K be a field of characteristic zero, A a K-algebra and δ a K-derivation or K-E-derivation of A. Then the following two statements hold: A) If δ is LF, then for all idempotents e ∈ Im δ, the principle ideal (e) is contained in Im δ; B) If δ is LN, then for all ϑ-ideal I of A and all idempotents e ∈ δ(I), the ϑ-ideal (e)ϑ is contained in δ(I).

accepted.question_text: Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let (Λ, ∗) be a monoid with unit element e. Suppose A has a K-algebra grading A = ⊕_{λ∈Λ} A_λ such that each A_λ is a K-subspace of A and A_λ A_μ ⊆ A_{λ∗μ} for all λ, μ in Λ. Must the K-subspace formed by all non-unit homogeneous pieces, namely ⊕_{e≠λ∈Λ} A_λ, always be a Mathieu subspace of A?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.1. (The Grading Conjecture) Let K be a field of characteristic zero (not necessarily algebraically closed), A a K-algebra and (Λ, ∗) a monoid with the unit e. Assume that A has the following K-algebra grading with respect to the monoid (Λ, ∗): (4.4) A = ⊕_{λ∈Λ} A_λ, i.e., A_λ is a K-subspace of A for each λ ∈ Λ, and A_λA_μ ⊆ A_{λ∗μ} for all λ, μ ∈ Λ. Then the K-subspace ⊕_{e≠λ∈Λ} A_λ is a MS of A.

accepted.question_text: Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let z = (z_1, z_2, ..., z_n) be commutative or noncommutative free variables. In the Laurent polynomial algebra A[z^{-1}, z], let M be the K-subspace consisting of all Laurent polynomials whose constant term is zero. Must M always be a Mathieu subspace of A[z^{-1}, z]?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.4. Let K be a field of characteristic zero, A a K-algebra, and z = (z1, z2, . . . , zn) n commutative or noncommutative free variables. Denote by M the K-subspace of the Laurent polynomial algebra A[z^{-1}, z] consisting of the Laurent polynomials with no constant term. Then M is a MS of A[z^{-1}, z].
